newsitem.title: IRAN: Masood forces claim control of north Afghan town.
newsitem.headline: Masood forces claim control of north Afghan town.

text.p: The forces of Afghan opposition commander Ahmad Shah Masood said they remained in control of a strategic town north of Kabul after repulsing an offensive by the Taleban militia, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Sunday.

The Taleban had said on Saturday its forces recaptured Jabal os-Siraj, 70 km (44 miles) from Kabul, in an early morning attack and were advancing further in an apparent move to clear the main highway to the opposition-held north.

IRNA quoted a spokesman for Masood forces as saying his forces "repulsed an offensive launched by the Taleban in Jabal os-Seraj...killing tens of Taleban forces and capturing a large number of others."

"During the counter-offensive in which aircraft and helicopters of the anti-Taliban forces were deployed, Taleban forces sustained casualties and fled to the surrounding areas," IRNA quoted the spokesman as telling it.
"The Jabal os-Seraj region is presently under the control of of Masood's forces," the spokesman said. "The forces are prepared to defend it."
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the conflicting reports.
Jabal os-Siraj controls access to the Salang highway that leads to the north over the towering Hindu Kush mountains.
